qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Gas turbine oligopoly (GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries) commanding >60% of the global heavy-duty market. Moat anchored in massive installed base (>7,000 gas turbines) locked into 10-25 year CPI-indexed Contractual Service Agreements (CSAs) with extreme switching costs. High-temperature materials science (single-crystal superalloys, thermal barrier coatings) and regulatory certification create insurmountable barriers to new entrants. Primary erosion risks: long-term decarbonization of the electric grid replacing gas peakers/baseload, rapid wind turbine technology obsolescence, and cyclical customer capex cutbacks.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). While GE Vernova enjoys a strong near-term cyclical boom from AI data center power demand and grid electrification, its business model fails the 15+ year predictable runway requirement. Heavy Electrical Equipment is anchored in Tier 3 (10-15Y baseline), and the company faces severe long-term terminal headwinds from Macrotrend 4 (Energy Transition): thermal gas turbines, its core cash cow, face regulatory net-zero phase-outs and long-term substitution by renewables, storage, and nuclear over a 15-30 year horizon. Additionally, its offshore wind division has suffered acute execution and contract inflation volatility, reflecting the capital-intensive cyclicality of heavy industrial equipment.
qualitative.evidence: Spun off from GE in April 2024. Power segment benefits from an installed base of >7,000 gas turbines with multi-decade CSAs, driving 2024 revenue of $34.9B, net income of $1.6B, FCF of $1.7B, and 12.3% ROIC. FY 2025 saw revenue grow to $38.1B, FCF of $3.7B, and ROIC of 25.2% (aided by a $2.9B valuation allowance release), with total backlog expanding to $150B on surging AI data center baseload power and grid equipment demand. However, historical pre-spin 5-10 year median ROIC was ~7.5% due to deep cyclical downturns and massive wind turbine operating losses (-$1B+ annually in 2022-2023). Long-term terminal value remains exposed to the 15-30 year decarbonization horizon for fossil gas generation and severe cyclicality in heavy capital goods orders.
